tests.title: Question bank – 1.1 Meaning and Importance of Financial Literacy

questions.question_text: Which statement best separates financial inclusion from financial literacy?
options: Both mean the same thing, as access to a product always brings understanding of it
Inclusion means teaching people about money, while literacy means giving loans to the poor
Inclusion is understanding how to use financial products, while literacy is simply holding a bank account
Inclusion is access to affordable products such as accounts and insurance, while literacy is understanding how to use them

questions.question_text: The OECD/INFE definition of financial literacy combines awareness, knowledge, skills and which other elements?
options: Income and assets needed to make sound financial decisions
Tax slabs and insurance covers needed to make sound decisions
Attitudes and behaviours needed to make sound financial decisions
Credit scores and bank balances needed to make sound decisions

questions.question_text: Financial education differs from financial literacy in that financial education is:
options: The result of understanding products, whereas literacy is the teaching process
The regulation of banks, whereas literacy is the regulation of insurers
The process of imparting the knowledge, whereas literacy is the resulting understanding
The act of opening accounts, whereas literacy is the act of borrowing

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT usually listed as an importance of financial literacy?
options: It helps people plan income, expenses, savings and debt
It guarantees a fixed return on every investment made by the person
It protects people from frauds, scams and Ponzi schemes
It reduces dependence on informal moneylenders

questions.question_text: Greater household financial literacy supports the wider economy mainly by:
options: Raising household savings and deepening the financial markets
Increasing the rate of inflation in the economy
Lowering the number of bank branches in a country
Removing the need for any financial regulator

questions.question_text: A family learns to track expenses, keep an emergency fund and avoid unsecured high-interest loans. Which importance of financial literacy does this show?
options: Better planning of income, savings and debt, and lower risk of over-indebtedness
Automatic improvement of the rate of return on all investments
Complete protection against rises in prices

questions.question_text: Which body's view describes financial literacy as the ability to make informed judgements and take effective decisions about the use and management of money?
options: RBI and the National Centre for Financial Education
The Goods and Services Tax Council

questions.question_text: Learning about frauds and phishing before using UPI is an example of which benefit of financial literacy?
options: Lower income tax for every person
Safe use of digital payment tools and protection against fraud
Free insurance cover for every person

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a direct result of better credit behaviour that financial literacy promotes?
options: A guaranteed pension from the government
Exemption from paying any loan instalment
A higher bank deposit insurance limit
A higher credit score and easier access to loans on better terms

questions.question_text: Which statement about financial inclusion is correct?
options: It means access to affordable products like a bank account, credit, insurance and pension for all, especially weaker sections
It is a tax benefit available only to salaried employees
It is the process by which investors are taught about shares
It is the same as personal budgeting
